column2: On the authority of Abū Mālik al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀṣim al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Purification is half of faith. Al-ḥamdu lillāh (praise be to Allah) fills the Balance,

and subḥān Allāh (glory be to Allah) and al-ḥamdu lillāh fill—or: fills—what is between the heavens and the earth. Prayer is light, charity is proof, patience is radiance, and the Qurʾān is an argument for you or against you. Every person goes out in the morning and sells himself, either freeing it or destroying it.” Reported by Muslim.

Purification (al-ṭuhūr) has been explained as leaving shirk, sins and acts of disobedience and ridding oneself of them; it has also been explained as wuḍūʾ for prayer, with faith (īmān) explained as prayer, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: “And Allah would not let your faith go to waste” [al-Baqarah 2:143], that is,

your prayer towards Jerusalem. The explanation of al-ṭuhūr as wuḍūʾ is supported by al-Tirmidhī's narration of the hadith (3517), which has “wuḍūʾ” instead of “purification”, and Ibn Mājah's narration (280) with the wording “Performing wuḍūʾ thoroughly”.
Al-shaṭr has been explained as “half”, and also as “a part”, even if not a half. Wuḍūʾ is a condition of prayer, as the hadith says: “No prayer is accepted without purification,

nor charity from stolen spoils.” Reported by Muslim (224). Ṭuhūr, with a u (ḍammah), is a noun for the act, namely purifying oneself, and ṭahūr, with an a (fatḥah), is a noun for the water with which one purifies oneself; the words wuḍūʾ, suḥūr, wujūr and suʿūṭ are likewise.

His words, “Al-ḥamdu lillāh fills the Balance, and subḥān Allāh and al-ḥamdu lillāh fill—or: fills—what is between the heavens and the earth”: the Balance is the Balance of deeds. This shows the virtue of praising (taḥmīd) and glorifying (tasbīḥ). Glorifying is declaring Allah free of every deficiency, and praising is describing Him with every perfection.

His words, “fill—or: fills”, may mean that it is glorifying and praising together that fill what is between the heavens and the earth, or only one of them; and it may be that filling what is between the heaven and the earth belongs to both together, the report reflecting the narrator's doubt over whether the verb was dual or not.
His words, “Prayer is light”, include light in the heart, light in the face, the light of guidance and light on the Day of Resurrection.
His words, “charity is proof”, mean evidence of its giver's faith and truthfulness,

because souls are tight-fisted with wealth, so when someone is saved from his own soul's tight-fistedness and gives charity, that is a sign of his faith; and because a hypocrite may pray to show off, but his soul will not let him give charity, because of his miserliness and greed for wealth.
His words, “patience is radiance”, mean patience in acts of obedience even if they are hard on the soul, in refraining from acts of disobedience even if the soul inclines to them,

and with the painful decrees of Allah, without panic or resentment. When this is found in a Muslim, it shows the strength of his faith and the light of his insight, and that is why patience is described as radiance.

His words, “and the Qurʾān is an argument for you or against you”, mean that the Qurʾān is either an argument for a person, if he fulfils what is obligatory on him and what is required of him in the Qurʾān—believing its reports, carrying out its commands, avoiding its prohibitions and reciting it as it deserves to be recited—

or an argument against him, if he turns away from it and does not fulfil what is required of him. Similar to this hadith are his words ﷺ in the hadith reported by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (817): “Allah raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it.”
His words, “Every person goes out in the morning and sells himself, either freeing it or destroying it”, mean that people go out in the morning and strive, and they divide into two groups:

one group sells itself to Allah by doing acts of obedience and avoiding acts of disobedience, thereby freeing itself from the Fire and keeping itself far from the devil's attempts to mislead and seduce it; and another group destroys itself by committing sins and acts of disobedience,
falling into unlawful desires that lead it to the Fire.
An explanation of the virtue of purification.
An explanation of the virtue of praising and glorifying [Allah].
Affirmation of the Balance and the weighing of deeds.
The virtue of prayer, and that it is light in this world and the Hereafter.
The virtue of charity, and that it is a sign of its giver's faith.
The virtue of patience, and that it is radiance for the patient.
Encouragement to devote attention to the Qurʾān by learning it, reflecting on it and acting on it,
so that it is an argument for a person.
A warning against falling short in what is owed to the Qurʾān,
lest it be an argument against him.
Encouragement to do every righteous deed by which a person frees himself from disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.
A warning against every bad deed that makes its doer one of the allies of the devil and leads him to the Fire.
